feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid public-sector specialization. It reads polished and substantive, but it is slightly dense and somewhat repetitive across sections, which reduces impact and scanability.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative with strong career progression at NACo, culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good use of scale and credibility signals: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms strengthen trust.  
- Writing is professional and mostly error-free, with a modern positioning around AI-enabled search, digital modernization, and cross-channel communications.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Recent Projects” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would sharpen structure and save space.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond scope/responsibility. Several bullets describe what you led or built, but fewer show measurable business or audience impact.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma, and capitalization is uneven (“Coleman DAVIS” vs. standard title case). No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “Senior digital leader” with a more specific positioning tied to public-sector digital transformation and communications systems.
- Add one concrete proof point from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Tighten the list of responsibilities into fewer, sharper themes: web modernization, governance/editorial systems, analytics, and AI-enabled discovery.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital platform and communications systems leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web transformation, governance and editorial operations, analytics infrastructure, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled content discovery for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” duplicates the subtitle; vary the wording.
- The long capability list repeats Core Competencies and Topline Skills almost verbatim.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but this section overlaps heavily with the summary and Topline Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating broader skill categories.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Prioritize the most senior/recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, and multimedia operations.
- Consider a sharper version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space is tight, replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” for more specificity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and all four Topline Skills sections.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” and “Multi-channel communications operations” are already well covered in Work Experience.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently repeats themes already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense for a footer. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope where possible would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in like “Selected Recent Projects” and format each item as a compact one-line achievement for easier scanning.
- Tighten wording: e.g., “AI-powered legislative search” instead of “AI-enabled legislative search experience,” and “site-integrated 10x20-foot interactive conference display” for clarity.
- Standardize style and punctuation across entries; use parallel verbs (“Designed,” “Built,” “Developed,” “Launched/Produced”).
- If space allows, add one concrete result, audience, or scale detail to 1–2 projects to increase specificity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and the advocacy video series substantially overlap with current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- The anniversary campaign may be the best differentiator because it adds a distinctive cross-channel example not fully covered elsewhere.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Core Competencies

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, leadership, and the highest-value themes that aren’t already covered elsewhere in the CV.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client context: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization, strengthening enterprise communications across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Combine overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one sharper line: “Built cross-functional workflows, governance standards, and analytics systems to improve coordination, publishing consistency, and decision-making.”
- Make the Drupal/campaign bullet more outcome-led: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users, publishers, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search improvement metrics, or engagement gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” overlaps with the Recent Projects section; keep this bullet brief unless you remove or shorten the footer project.
- Governance/analytics/platform modernization also echo the NACo role, so emphasize what is new here: consulting scope, enterprise advisory work, and current AI/search leadership.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It can be sharper by foregrounding the biggest outcomes, tightening channel-management language, and avoiding overlap with earlier NACo roles on newsletters/video.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, overseeing web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the website bullets into one outcome-led line: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make analytics and operations more results-oriented: add any measurable gains such as reporting speed, stakeholder adoption, publishing efficiency, or decision-making cadence.
- Tighten channel language: replace “reaching tens of thousands” / “serving thousands” with exact subscriber/follower counts if available; otherwise keep this brief.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Managed newsletters” and “video programming” overlap with the Associate Communications Director role; in this entry, emphasize enterprise leadership, platform modernization, governance, and analytics.
- “Built in-house video studio” may partially overlap with footer projects; keep this bullet focused on organizational capability built, not content series.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing operational leadership, editorial coordination, and channel growth before the larger-scale platform/governance work in 2022–2024.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and measurable if possible: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.” Add views, cadence, or audience growth if available.
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper point: “Built cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows that improved coordination, consistency and turnaround across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent roles. It should be tighter and more differentiated, emphasizing leadership scope rather than repeating generic digital/content terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more specific, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy and governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel” for “Cross-channel” and “Audience-focused” for “Audience strategy” to sound more senior and concise.
- If space allows, add one sharper leadership signal such as “organization-wide communications planning” or “50+ publisher governance” drawn from recent experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “governance,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially repeat the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to web modernization and platform delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery” instead of listing platforms flatly.
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths: Drupal, CMS modernization, API integrations, workflow automation, AI-enabled search; de-emphasize older/basic items like jQuery.
- Tighten and group related items for scanability, e.g. “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” and “SharePoint/Power Pages.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills more strategic and save full tool lists for Technical + IT.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; consider using “search and discovery systems” here to reduce repetition.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design

- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic to justify its place in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Keep only the most relevant tools and group them: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Tighten wording and show application: “Dashboarding and insight generation for leadership decision-making” instead of just “Leadership reporting.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating every tool elsewhere; let this section emphasize strategic analytics capability, while Technical + IT holds the full stack.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability and recent in-house studio/event leadership rather than basic task skills.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more outcome-oriented, senior phrasing:
- Broadcast-quality video production & post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- In-house studio buildout and operations
- PTZ/multi-camera production systems
- Consider renaming the heading to “Video, Studio & Event Production” for clarity and stronger alignment with recent leadership work.
- If space allows elsewhere, add scale/context instead of more tools, e.g., “recurring advocacy programming” or “in-house broadcast studio leadership.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies.
- Avoid listing low-level tools here if Premiere Pro and related tools already appear in Technical + IT.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” In this section, make it more specific and weighted toward the most relevant/recent platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strength/relevance: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages** • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: **Drupal (10, enterprise/public-sector)** • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** unless it reflects meaningful production use; it reads lighter than the others.
- Keep this item platform-only; avoid adding CMS modernization or technical implementation terms already covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the “Topline Skills” entry **Web Platforms & Technical Execution** almost exactly; either consolidate or make this version more tool-focused and the other more capability-focused.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so emphasize it here rather than giving equal weight to all platforms.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and, where possible, emphasize current/recent tools.

Suggested edit:
- Retitle or tighten to stress hands-on delivery: “Front-End & Technical Implementation” or “Technical Implementation.”
- Rewrite for specificity and consistency: “HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, REST/API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”
- Consider grouping by function for faster scanning: “Front-end: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery | Integrations: REST/API integrations, GTM | Dev/automation: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”
- If space allows elsewhere, connect 1–2 tools to outcomes in recent roles instead of listing only technologies (e.g., GTM for analytics deployment, Cloudflare Workers for lightweight web functionality).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may also overlap conceptually with analytics tooling; keep it here only if positioned as implementation, not reporting.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already highlighted elsewhere. Make it more purposeful by grouping tools by function and emphasizing automation/integration platforms over general collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Workflow design • Cross-platform automation • Project systems: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Collaboration: Slack, Teams**
- Put the highest-value tools first: lead with Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier since they best support your automation/systems positioning.
- Replace some app names with capability language where possible, e.g., “workflow design” or “cross-platform automation,” to sound more strategic.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie these tools to outcomes in recent roles rather than expanding this list here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools; they add less differentiation than automation/integration platforms.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. It should signal level of use and align with the CV’s stronger story around enterprise communications operations.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- If accurate, add scope/level: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (enterprise journeys, segmentation, automation) • Higher Logic (member communications/community engagement) • Mailchimp (campaign email)
- Keep platform names only if this section is meant to be a skills inventory; otherwise add a short qualifier such as “administration, campaign setup, audience segmentation.”
- Order by strongest/recent relevance; if Dynamics 365 was not used materially in recent roles, move Higher Logic first or remove the weakest platform.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with repeated email-channel claims in multiple NACo roles; avoid restating newsletter management here unless you add platform-specific depth.
- “Engagement” is vague and may duplicate “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” It should either be tightened to emphasize execution-level tools/methods or reduced to avoid repeating the same analytics story already proven in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI dashboard development
- Replace broad terms like “SEO” and “Dashboarding” with more concrete capabilities/tools; “Google Search Console” is stronger if accurate.
- Order by strongest/recently evidenced tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.
- If space allows, add one qualifier in the section heading or elsewhere: “Analytics Tools & Optimization” to make the list feel more specific.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider keeping the fuller version in one place and shortening this to tools only.
- “A/B testing” is not evidenced elsewhere in the CV; keep only if you can support it in experience/interviews.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads like a setup role rather than showing concrete contributions. Tighten it around team-building, platform work, and recurring multimedia outputs, with metrics if you can add them.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and scope: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Split the second sentence into clearer achievements: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- Replace “high-impact” with evidence: add counts, audience size, frequency, or engagement gains if available.
- Clarify supervision: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “mentored one digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating “weekly video update” too heavily since the 2018–2022 role already emphasizes expanding that program.
- “Strengthening workflows” overlaps with later entries; keep this version focused on helping establish the team and early execution.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or scope, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize the standout achievement first: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer action: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audiences served, cross-functional teams supported, or types of programs/policy areas covered.
- Keep this entry lighter than later roles; position it as a foundation in research + multimedia rather than full digital leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later video/media roles; keep this item focused on podcast launch and program/policy support.
- Avoid repeating broad digital leadership language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software, workflows, and production capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so it should be tightened to emphasize tools only.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Creative & Production Tools” or “Multimedia Tools” for clarity.
- Separate software from capabilities; keep this line tool-focused.
- Suggested rewrite: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator”
- If you want to retain production capabilities, move them to the existing skills section and rewrite there as: “Livestream studio operations • Podcast production”
